evidence_rows.lay_context: Macrophages and T cells are both types of immune cells, but the drug only worked to stop the virus in the macrophages.
allowed_evidence_spans: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells
forbidden_overgeneralizations: SFN blocks HIV in all immune cells

high_risk_check_facts.fact: SFN blocks HIV in macrophages but not T cells.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Removing Nrf2 increases HIV infection and reduces SFN's effectiveness.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Depletion of Nrf2 using siRNA increases HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and diminishes the protective effects of Sulforaphane (SFN).
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Importantly this block is indeed dependent on Nrf2.
evidence_rows.lay_context: When researchers used a technique called siRNA to remove the Nrf2 protein, the virus was able to infect the cells more easily.
allowed_evidence_spans: siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 boosted HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and reduced the anti-viral effects of SFN treatment
forbidden_overgeneralizations: Nrf2 is the only thing that stops HIV

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Depletion of Nrf2 boosted HIV infectivity.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: boosted HIV infectivity

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: SFN blocks HIV after it enters the cell but before it forms specific DNA structures.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Sulforaphane (SFN) treatment inhibits HIV infection at a stage after the virus enters the cell but before the formation of 2-LTR circles.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: the virus is blocked after it has transcribed its RNA-encoded genome into DNA, but before this genetic material is inserted into host chromosomes.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The virus can still get inside the cell, but the treatment stops it before it can finish preparing its genetic material to hide in the cell's DNA.
allowed_evidence_spans: blocks infection after entry , but before formation of 2-LTR circles
forbidden_overgeneralizations: SFN prevents HIV from entering the cell

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The block occurs before the formation of 2-LTR circles.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: before formation of 2-LTR circles

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The block does not use common anti-viral proteins like SAMHD1 or MX2.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The anti-viral effect of Nrf2 activation against HIV does not involve the upregulation of known anti-viral proteins SAMHD1 or MX2.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Interestingly, Nrf2 does not activate recognized anti-viral genes.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Usually, the body uses specific proteins like SAMHD1 to fight HIV, but Nrf2 seems to use a different, unknown pathway.
allowed_evidence_spans: neither SAMHD1 nor MX2 were upregulated
SFN did not significantly change levels of either SAMHD1 or MX2

high_risk_check_facts.fact: SAMHD1 and MX2 levels were not increased by SFN.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: neither SAMHD1 nor MX2 were upregulated

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Nrf2 activation is a novel way to potently block HIV infection.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Understanding how to activate cellular anti-viral defenses like Nrf2 may provide new therapeutic alternatives to current anti-retroviral treatments.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This highlights the opportunity to activate a heretofore unrecognized anti-viral function by triggering an antioxidant response.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This discovery suggests that drugs or supplements that trigger the body's antioxidant response could be a new way to treat HIV.
allowed_evidence_spans: new therapeutic alternatives to overcome these limitations
SFN , and other Nrf2 stimulators , could be used therapeutically
forbidden_overgeneralizations: Nrf2 is a cure for HIV

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: A dengue epidemic in the Dominican Republic was immediately followed by a Zika outbreak, allowing for a comparative study.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: A major dengue outbreak in the Dominican Republic in 2015 and early 2016 was immediately followed by the appearance of Zika virus cases.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: In 2015–2016, the Dominican Republic was struck by an epidemic of dengue followed by an outbreak of Zika.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Both viruses are spread by Aedes mosquitoes and belong to the same family (flaviviruses), making their back-to-back appearance a unique case for study.
allowed_evidence_spans: In Dominican Republic , the appearance of Zika virus cases that closely followed a large dengue epidemic provided an opportunity to study the different transmission drivers behind these two flaviviruses.
forbidden_overgeneralizations: Zika and dengue always occur together

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The dengue epidemic occurred in 2015 and early 2016.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: In 2015–2016, the Dominican Republic was struck by an epidemic of dengue

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Dengue primarily affected youth, while Zika was more evenly distributed across age groups.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Approximately 75% of dengue cases in the Dominican Republic occurred before the age of 20, whereas only about 42% of Zika cases occurred in that same age group.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Zika cases were much higher among sexually active age groups.
evidence_rows.lay_context: While dengue is often a childhood illness in areas where it is common, Zika affected a broader range of adults.
allowed_evidence_spans: 75% of all dengue cases occurred before the age of 20 compared with ~42 for Zika.
Zika infections were more widely dispersed among the population.

high_risk_check_facts.fact: 75% of dengue cases were in people under 20.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: 75% of all dengue cases occurred before the age of 20

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Zika infections were significantly more common in females than in males.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Zika infection rates in the Dominican Republic were markedly higher among women (73.8%) than among men (26.2%).
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Zika cases were much higher among females.
evidence_rows.lay_context: This sharp difference between sexes was much more pronounced for Zika than for dengue.
allowed_evidence_spans: Zika infection was markedly lower among men than women: 26 . 2% ... vs . 73 . 8%

high_risk_check_facts.fact: 73.8% of Zika cases were in females.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Despite higher Zika reports in women, a related neurological condition was slightly more common in men.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS) attack rates were slightly higher in males than in females, despite higher reported Zika rates in females.
evidence_rows.lay_context: GBS is a rare but serious condition where the immune system attacks the nerves, sometimes triggered by Zika.
allowed_evidence_spans: GBS attack rates stratified by sex revealed slightly higher risk in males vs . females , at 0 . 62 and 0 . 57 per 10 , 000 population respectively.
forbidden_overgeneralizations: GBS is more common than Zika

high_risk_check_facts.fact: GBS rate was 0.62 per 10,000 in males.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: 0 . 62 ... per 10 , 000 population

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Prior dengue immunity did not seem to protect the population from Zika.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Existing population-level immunity to dengue appeared to have little impact on Zika attack rates.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: prior dengue infections ... had no material impact on the likelihood of reporting Zika illness
evidence_rows.lay_context: Scientists were concerned that having had dengue might change how people react to Zika, but this data suggests it didn't change the overall infection rates.
allowed_evidence_spans: Evidence suggests little impact of existing dengue immunity on reported attack rates of Zika at the population level.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The high number of Zika cases in women is likely due to health-seeking behavior rather than biology.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The higher reported incidence of Zika among women may be driven by increased health-seeking behavior and community awareness rather than biological susceptibility.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: it is most likely that the clustering of cases among women was the result of health-seeking behaviour caused by health campaigns
evidence_rows.lay_context: Because Zika can cause birth defects, media campaigns specifically warned women, which likely led more women to visit doctors and get tested than men.
allowed_evidence_spans: community awareness campaigns , through influencing short-term health seeking behaviour , remain the most plausible mechanism behind increased reporting among women
forbidden_overgeneralizations: Women are more likely to get sick

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Health-seeking behavior is the most plausible mechanism for the sex difference.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: most plausible mechanism behind increased reporting among women

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Anabaena filaments develop a pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts under nitrogen deprivation.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Under nitrogen deprivation, filaments of the cyanobacterium Anabaena develop a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by approximately ten photosynthetic vegetative cells.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Anabaena forms a pattern of specialized nitrogen-fixing cells (heterocysts) separated by about ten vegetative cells.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Anabaena is a type of multicellular cyanobacteria that forms long chains or filaments of cells.
allowed_evidence_spans: Under nitrogen deprivation , filaments of the cyanobacterium Anabaena undergo a process of development , resulting in a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Heterocysts are separated by about ten vegetative cells.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The study used a hetR-gfp fusion to track the expression of the essential transcription factor HetR.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The transcription factor HetR is essential for the differentiation of heterocysts in Anabaena filaments.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Researchers used a fluorescent marker to follow the expression of the regulator HetR in individual cells.
evidence_rows.lay_context: HetR is a master regulator protein that acts like a switch to tell cells when to become heterocysts.
allowed_evidence_spans: HetR , a transcription factor essential for heterocyst differentiation
chromosomal hetR-gfp fusion , thereby avoiding any contribution to fluctuations stemming from cell-cell variability in plasmid copy number

high_risk_check_facts.fact: HetR is a transcription factor essential for differentiation.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: HetR , a transcription factor essential for heterocyst differentiation

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby cells are coupled across a range of two to three cells.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Fluctuations in the expression of the hetR gene in nearby cells are coupled with a spatial range of approximately two to three cells.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The study establishes the spatial extent to which gene expression is correlated along filaments.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Even when cells are identical, their gene activity can fluctuate randomly; this study found these fluctuations are linked between neighbors.
allowed_evidence_spans: expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby cells are coupled , with a characteristic spatial range of circa two to three cells

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The spatial range of coupling is two to three cells.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: circa two to three cells

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Correlations arise primarily from intercellular molecular transfer.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Correlations in gene expression between cells in Anabaena filaments arise primarily from intercellular molecular transfer rather than cell division.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The developmental program uses transport to create spatial patterns.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Cells communicate by passing molecules to one another through specialized channels.
allowed_evidence_spans: Correlations between cells predominantly arise from intercellular molecular transfer and less from cell division .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Molecular transfer is the dominant cause of correlations.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: predominantly arise from intercellular molecular transfer

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Fluctuations after nitrogen deprivation build on those present in nitrogen-rich conditions.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Gene expression fluctuations observed after nitrogen deprivation build upon primordial fluctuations already present under nitrogen-rich conditions.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The developmental program plays a role even under non-inducing conditions.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The patterns seen during starvation actually start as small variations while the bacteria are still well-fed.
allowed_evidence_spans: fluctuations found once the developmental network has been triggered , build up from those under nitrogen-rich conditions .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: PatS, SepJ, and HetR auto-regulation determine fluctuations under nitrogen-rich conditions.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The inhibitor PatS, the septal protein SepJ, and positive HetR auto-regulation are essential determinants of hetR expression fluctuations under nitrogen-rich conditions.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Positive feedback, lateral inhibition and cell-cell communication play a role before the external trigger.
evidence_rows.lay_context: PatS acts as a brake (inhibitor), while SepJ helps with communication between cells.
allowed_evidence_spans: HetR inhibitor PatS , cell-cell communication influenced by the septal protein SepJ and positive HetR auto-regulation are essential determinants

high_risk_check_facts.fact: PatS is an inhibitor of HetR.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: HetR inhibitor PatS

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The study highlights differences between inhibitors PatS and HetN, and septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The study examined various mutant strains lacking regulatory genes patS, hetN, and hetR, or septal protein genes sepJ, fraC, and fraD to compare their roles.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The analysis brings out the different roles and specificity of inter-cellular communication proteins.
evidence_rows.lay_context: By removing specific proteins (creating 'mutants'), scientists can see how each part of the communication system works.
allowed_evidence_spans: differences between the two HetR inhibitors PatS and HetN , as well as the differences in specificity between the septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: FraC and FraD are septal proteins.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: septal proteins FraC and FraD

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Communication proteins combine with stochasticity to control developmental patterns.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Inter-cellular communication proteins play distinct roles in setting spatial correlations of gene expression to control noise and avoid erroneous cell fates.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The developmental program uses communication to create patterns in the presence of unavoidable stochastic fluctuations.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Biological systems are naturally 'noisy' or random; cells use communication to manage this noise and make the right developmental choices.
allowed_evidence_spans: multicellular organisms can use cell-cell communication in order to control noise in gene expression
control the coupled fluctuations of gene expression that give rise to a one-dimensional developmental pattern

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings through dual-adaptation.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings (dual-adaptation) when feedback for each is provided alternately.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Humans generally make use of previous experiences to determine the best course of action, such as adjusting behavior for geometric distortions.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Visuomotor mapping refers to how our brain coordinates what we see with how we move, like adjusting your aim when wearing glasses that distort your vision.
allowed_evidence_spans: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings ( dual-adaptation ) when feedback for each is provided alternately .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: humans can only learn one mapping at a time

high_risk_check_facts.fact: dual-adaptation occurs when feedback is provided alternately
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: when feedback for each is provided alternately

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Participants performed a target-pointing task with manipulated visual feedback offsets.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Participants performed a rapid target-pointing task on a graphics tablet while their view of their own arm was obstructed to test visual feedback shifts.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The study used a target-pointing task where different target shapes were associated with different distortions.
evidence_rows.lay_context: To test how people adapt, researchers had them point at targets on a tablet while hiding their actual hand from view, then showing them a 'fake' cursor that was shifted to the side.
allowed_evidence_spans: prevented the participants from seeing their own arm
visual feedback was shifted by 75 mm to the right
forbidden_overgeneralizations: the task was slow and deliberate

high_risk_check_facts.fact: visual feedback was shifted by 75 mm
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: shifted by 75 mm to the right

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Target shapes ranged from spiky to circular on a continuous scale.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Target shapes were used as contextual cues that ranged from very spiky to completely round on a continuous scale.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Participants needed to aim right-of-target for spiky shapes and left-of-target for round ones.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The researchers used a series of shapes that gradually changed (morphed) from a circle to a spiky star-like shape to see if people could learn a rule based on the shape's appearance.
allowed_evidence_spans: ranged from very spiky to completely round
continuous scale

high_risk_check_facts.fact: shapes ranged from circular to spiky
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: ranged from circular to spiky

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: A Bayesian learning model predicts generalization consistent with categorization.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: A Bayesian learning model (Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters) predicts that humans combine new feedback with prior experience in a way that favors categorization over linear rules.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The model demonstrates that participants learn separate shape-response pairs rather than a general relationship.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Instead of figuring out a mathematical rule for all shapes, the model suggests people remember specific examples and pick the one that looks most like the current shape.
allowed_evidence_spans: Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters Model
Bayes-optimal learning

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters Model was used
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters Model

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Learning requires explicit awareness and follows similarity-based mapping.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Learning the associations requires conscious awareness of the cue's role, and participants apply the mapping of the most similar trained shape.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Participants did not use the trained linear relationship, but weighed learned contexts by similarity.
evidence_rows.lay_context: People only learned the task if they consciously noticed that the shape mattered; once they did, they simply matched new shapes to the closest one they already knew.

trained shape that is most similar to the current one

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Learning slows down as the number of training pairs increases.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The learning rate decreases systematically as the number of shape-mapping pairs to be learned simultaneously increases due to interference.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Learning substantially slowed down with increased numbers of training shapes.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The more shape-and-aiming pairs the participants had to memorize at once, the longer it took them to learn, because the different shapes started to 'interfere' with each other in their memory.
allowed_evidence_spans: learning rate decreases systematically with the number of mappings
interfere with each other due to the generalisation of local learning
forbidden_overgeneralizations: more training pairs make learning faster
interference only happens with spiky shapes

high_risk_check_facts.fact: learning rate decreases as training pairs increase
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: learning rate decreases systematically with the number of mappings

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Resource constraints prevent many countries from scaling up NTD programs due to a lack of baseline data.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Resource constraints in endemic countries have hindered progress toward the control or elimination of five major neglected tropical diseases.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward control or elimination goals.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) cause physical debilitation and lowered economic productivity, but countries often lack the data needed to plan treatment programs.
allowed_evidence_spans: resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward these goals

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Five NTDs are targeted for control or elimination.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Researchers developed and field-tested the Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) methodology for multiple NTDs.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Researchers developed the Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) methodology to simultaneously map lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: We have developed an integrated mapping protocol, Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) for use by Ministries of Health.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The ITM methodology allows health officials to check for several different parasitic diseases at the same time.
allowed_evidence_spans: Integrated Threshold Mapping ( ITM ) Methodology ) for lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminths ( STH )

high_risk_check_facts.fact: The protocol covers LF, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and STH.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminths ( STH )

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The protocol determines if a threshold for public health intervention has been reached.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The ITM methodology is designed to determine if a threshold for public health intervention has been met rather than providing exact prevalence figures.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Decide where public health interventions for NTDs are needed.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Before starting mass drug treatments, a country must prove that the number of infected people has passed a specific limit set by health organizations.

does not provide prevalence figures
forbidden_overgeneralizations: measures exact number of sick people

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The protocol was tested against standard WHO methodologies in Mali and Senegal.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) methodology was field-tested in districts in Mali and Senegal and compared against standard WHO mapping methodologies.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: We compared this protocol to the World Health Organizations disease-specific mapping protocols in Mali and Senegal.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Researchers ran the new test alongside the current standard tests in West Africa to see if the results matched.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: ITM reached the same conclusions as WHO for most diseases but was more targeted for schistosomiasis.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as standard WHO methods for trachoma, LF, and STH, but resulted in more targeted recommendations for schistosomiasis.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Results from both methodologies indicated the same public health interventions for trachoma, LF and STH, while the ITM methodology resulted in a more targeted intervention for schistosomiasis.
evidence_rows.lay_context: For schistosomiasis, the new method identified specific smaller areas (sub-districts) that needed treatment, rather than treating an entire large district.
allowed_evidence_spans: reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies regarding the initiation of public health interventions for trachoma , LF and STH
more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: ITM was practical and demonstrated overall cost savings compared to standard methods.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The ITM methodology resulted in a 31% overall cost savings in Mali and a 19% overall cost savings in Senegal compared to the standard WHO methodology.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The integrated methodology is also less expensive and logistically more feasible to implement.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The new approach saved money by combining transport, staff, and field time for multiple diseases at once.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: This integrated tool could facilitate the implementation of programs in endemic countries.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) tool could help endemic countries implement necessary disease control programs.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Could replace disease-specific mapping protocols in resource-poor NTD-endemic countries.
evidence_rows.lay_context: By making mapping easier and cheaper, more countries can start the treatment programs needed to eliminate these diseases.
